title: Delphi research result
description: What `research_result` returns to a host agent (specs/066 §4; crates/delphi-core/src/research.rs). A claim's `knowledge_status` is never raised by its source being trusted (specs/052).

answer.description: The answer, not validated (specs/114 section 5). Its last line is its label and says what was done: `written by the scout from N claims, not validated` for Markdown the scout wrote from the kept claims and code checked (every statement ends with `[c-…]` claim markers; `Not found.` under a sub-question no claim answers), or `list of claims (no synthesis)` for the code-built list a run returns when no answer was written or none passed the check. Raw page text is never returned.

synthesis.description: How the answer was made (specs/114 section 5): `scout` when the scout's answer passed the check, `list` when the code-built list was used, `none` when the run kept no claim.

claims.description: How many claims the answer was written from.

attempts.description: Answer calls made: an answer the check rejects is written once more.

rejected.description: For each answer the check rejected, how many findings it made. Counts only.

known_before.description: What Delphi already held on the question before the run searched (specs/114 section 3), as the session that asked could have found it by searching, and nothing more: claim ids with their status and one-line statement, research topics that overlap, sources held with their age, pointers into the knowledge base. Compare with `claims` to see what the run added.

read_from_library.description: Pages the run read from the library and did not fetch (specs/114 section 3 item 4): the library held each as a public page, its text kept, checked within its recheck window.

plan.description: Who made the run's plan (specs/114 section 4): the scout's plan call, the fixed plan (that call failed or returned nothing usable), or the record of the topic the run continued.

sub_questions.description: The plan's sub-questions with their coverage when the run ended; empty under the fixed plan. A sub-question is covered when the claims tagged to it are stated by at least two origins, or when the plan marked it known. The uncovered ones are what a continued run searches for.

stopped.description: Why the run stopped sending queries (specs/114 section 4 item 5).

rounds.description: How many rounds of queries the run sent.

sources.description: Where the run's web results came from (specs/119 sections 13.1 and 13.2): `host`: the host's own search tool ran the planned queries and handed back what it found (the engines, when there are any, are asked only for what that left uncovered); the engines of [search]; or `local`: no query was sent to anyone, and the run read what Delphi holds and the addresses it already knew on the trusted list.

host_search.description: On a run whose source is the host (specs/119 section 2.1): how many queries the host was asked to search, and how many it handed back.

host_leads.description: On a run whose source is the host: the addresses the host handed back that are not on the trusted list. The daemon did not fetch them; the host may read them with its own tool and hand over what it found with record_research.

empty.description: Present only when the run kept no claim and met none the library held, or kept claims the library recorded none of (specs/124 section 14, S11, and section 19): why, and what to do next. Counted by code from what the run did; every word is one of a fixed list and no address, page text, provider text or host's word is in it. It is information: nothing reads it as a reason to fetch, trust, promote or permit anything. When the run also had nothing to write an answer from, `answer` is `text` and `next` in one line; when the answer is written from claims held before the run, `next` says so.

reason.description: The first of `causes`: the cause nearest a claim.

causes.description: Every cause the run counted, from the step nearest a claim to the one furthest from it. `claims_not_stored`: claims were drawn and the library kept no record of them, so none can be cited. `no_model_seat`: pages were fetched and no model could serve the scout to read them. `scout_call_failed`: the scout's page-reading call failed. `no_claims_on_pages`: pages were read and no claim with a quote found in the page was drawn. `pages_refused`: the library's keep step refused the pages. `trusted_fetch_failed`, `fetch_failed`: the daemon could not fetch pages on, or off, the trusted list (`why` counts the fixed word of each failure). `leads_unread`: addresses the host handed back that the daemon did not fetch (`host_leads`): those not on the trusted list, or, when the session is under the private-read mark, every one. `not_fetchable`: results outside what the fetcher reaches, kept as leads. `nothing_new`: results already read. `budget`: the step budget ran out. `host_fed_nothing`: the host handed back none of the queries it was asked. `queries_withheld`: queries the identifier guard withheld. `no_search_provider`, `credential_unresolved`, `search_failed` (every engine failed for a reason other than its key), `no_results` (the searches answered with nothing): as in the coverage report. `no_search_run`: no search was sent and none failed. `no_local_sources`: a local run with no source on the trusted list for the question. `plan_no_model_seat`, `plan_unusable`: the scout's plan call gave no plan, so the run used the fixed plan (the question itself, not sub-questions).

n.description: How many times, when the cause is a count.

why.description: On a failed fetch: how many failed for each fixed word. Never the fetcher's or the server's own text.

text.description: The causes in plain words, built by code.

next.description: One sentence on what to do next: something the asker or the operator does. Delphi does none of it by itself.

web_search.description: Whether any web search answered in the run. When none did, the answer's label ends with `no web search`.

planned_under_mark.description: The session or task that asked was under the private-read mark of specs/103 (specs/119 section 15). The run is the same as any other: each query was cleaned and passed the identifier guard, and the search log lists every query planned.

new_claims.description: Deduplicated staged candidates, not search hits.

library_claims.description: The library claims this run wrote or added an anchor to (specs/112 section 3): `library/claims/<id>.json`. A claim the library already held is listed here and not in `claims`; it gained an anchor and the topic. Each reads `noted` until the library's own rules say otherwise.

corroboration_pass.description: The corroboration pass of a survey or deep run (specs/098 section 7.5 item 5): how many public claims it looked for more support for, and how many queries it sent. A claim resting on a private source is never queried.

coverage.description: `thin` when the knowledge base and the trusted sources together gave fewer kept, cited claims than `[research] thin_below` (specs/098 section 7.5).

coverage_report.description: What each rung of the source ladder (specs/098 section 7.1) turned up and kept. A `reason` appears only on a rung that was searched and found nothing, or cannot be reached from inside; it is one word of a fixed list and never provider text.

counted.description: Kept, cited claims from the knowledge base and the trusted sources, after dedupe.

host_rungs.description: When thin: the rungs the host's own tools and connectors can take over.

leads_kept.description: Search results the fetcher would not reach, kept as noted leads.

retractions.description: Present only when `[research] retractions` is on (specs/101 section 4): the state of the local Retraction Watch snapshot, `retractions: current (...)`, `retractions: stale (...)` or `retractions: none loaded`.

search_log.description: A summary of, and a link to, the top-level `search_log` (specs/101 section 3). Every host research result carries it.

check_steps.description: Steps of the check, which has a budget of its own: a quarter of the run's, at least two (specs/112 section 4.4). Never counted in `steps`.

topic_id.description: The research topic the run's record is kept under (specs/112 section 2): `research/topics/<topic_id>/` in the workspace, or in the project's folder. `delphi research show <topic_id>` prints it.

signature.description: The identity line in the form chosen by [mcp] badge_style: the same string as `display`, kept for hosts that read it.

display.description: The one line a host prints first (specs/087 section 5.2): the badge, the name and `(role, via delphi)`, in the form [mcp] badge_style names and, for ansi, the colour pair [mcp] badge_mode names. On a Council result it is followed by the ruling card.

boundary_line.description: Advice: `── Name (role) takes over: reason ──`, for when the speaker changes (specs/087 section 5.4). A host may drop it.

return_line.description: Advice: the matching line for when control comes back.

search_log.description: What the run searched, of whom, when, and how much came back (specs/101 section 3). Written by the daemon: a host cannot add, edit or delete a line. It is private when any claim it served is, and a private log never leaves the install. It is information; nothing reads it as a reason to trust, promote or permit anything.

search_line.description: One search. `query` is the same redacted string that was sent; a search withheld because its claim rests on a private source has `withheld: private` and no `query`, and one withheld because it named one of the workspace's privacy identifiers and too little was left without it (spec 119 section 2.7) has `withheld: identifier` and no `query`. Every line the daemon ran balances: hits = duplicates + kept + the sum of not_kept.

source.description: Of whom: the knowledge base, the operator's trusted list, a host tool the host declared, or a provider. doi, archive and citation are reserved for later slices of spec 101.

via.description: The provider that answered a trusted-list search.

failed.description: The search itself failed, in one word of the fixed list.

declared.description: Reported by the host, not made by the daemon. Its kept is 0 and it counts as nothing.

run_by_host.description: Run by the host with its own search tool, for a query the run asked of it, and handed back with research_feed (specs/119 section 2.1 item 4). Its results on the trusted list were read by the daemon; the others are counted under not_kept as `lead` and were not fetched.

local.description: Not a search: the addresses on the trusted list that a local run already knew for the question (specs/119 section 13.2). It has no query, and it is not counted in `searches`.

search_flow.description: The lines the daemon ran, summed (a declared line and the knowledge-base line are not in it): found = duplicates_removed + kept + the sum of not_kept.

claim_id.description: The library claim this claim was written as (specs/112 section 3.1). Its status there is derived by the library and is not this run's `knowledge_status`.

licence.description: The first source's licence as the library records it (specs/119 section 6 item 1); `unknown` when it does not say.

sources.description: Each source the claim was found in, with its licence and how the library keeps it (full, excerpts, pointer; unknown when it cannot say).

knowledge_status.description: `corroborated`: three or more independent origins state it, counted by code (specs/098 section 7.6). Weaker than `validated`; it raises nothing else and is never read as a reason to trust or permit anything.

corroboration.description: How many independent origins state the claim and how many of them are trusted sources (the operator's list inside its topic scope, or a Primary or Reputable class). Display only: it changes no status, taint, tier or queue order.

from_trusted_source.description: Provenance only; does not change knowledge_status.

sub_question.description: The number of the plan's sub-question the claim is tagged to (specs/114 section 4 item 3), when it has one.

counter_evidence.description: The claim was first read on a page a contradiction query returned (specs/114 section 4 item 7). A tag; it changes no status.

hex_light.description: The colour for a light terminal (specs/087 section 5.1).

via.description: Present when a host adopted the role. It does not change how the identity reads: the line always ends `, via delphi)` (specs/087 section 5.3).
